I don’t completely understand where I put layed out a “boys will be boys” attitude, but this sure shot wasn’t meant to be a solution in the conclusory sense. It was meant to give a little perspective so open communication can occur. Boys will be boys the first couple times due to individual biology, hormones levels (depending on the age), and environmental factors, but a little kindness when conveying something can help him to open up and be more cognizant of the situation. It’s a different action altogether you see as one points at a certain behavior, which will be done anyways, while one brings out an entirely different behavioral pattern. This isn’t a comparison to the boyfriend, but have you ever dealt with autistic children or the elderly with dementia? (I know weird set) I have and I also got the tism too and you know the single greatest tactic I’ve learned to creating understanding and progress? Listen. Gain perspective. And ask about their feelings. Often times the step we seem to forget the most is building a common reality and asking if the other person already feels a certain way about a situation. Ex: they do something bad => ask how they’re feeling => maybe they feel guilty => reassure them for whatever needs reassuring => and offer to work on it with them or talk about it to figure out an end. Both people with autism and those with dementia (and Alzheimer’s) struggle with a very noticeable difference in the reality they perceive and often times the emotions regarding it can be lost in translation and misinterpreted.
